newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli PM aide denies report of scandal charges.
newsitem.headline: Israeli PM aide denies report of scandal charges.

text.p: Israeli Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh dismissed a newspaper report on Tuesday that police probing alleged government corruption were struggling over whether to recommend charges against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Police later in the day were expected to present recommendations from their investigation into the ill-fated appointment in January of Roni Bar-On, a lawyer and activist in Netanyahu's Likud party, as attorney general.
Israel's Yedioth Ahronoth daily said police had new evidence pointing to Netanyahu's alleged involvement. Some politicians have said the affair could threaten the government.

"I've said all along during the investigation of this affair that I am sure and convinced the prime minister's hands are clean. I am sure and convinced of it also this morning as we speak," Netanyahu confidant Naveh told Israel's army radio.
All under investigation have denied any wrongdoing.

"Lately there has been a new development in the affair, in that new findings have come into the hands of investigators that strengthen, in their view, the evidence against the prime minister," the mass circulation Yedioth Ahronoth said.
"It is known that in light of the new evidence, police investigators are struggling now over whether to recommend that fraud and violation of trust charges be brought against Netanyahu," it said.

Police refused to comment on the newspaper report, but a spokeswoman said investigators would probably present recommendations on Tuesday to the state prosecutor, who makes the final decision on bringing charges.
Naveh slammed the stream of leaks to the media: "I regret these biased leaks which are only interested in trampling the good name of the prime minister."
He also dismissed reports Netanyahu's director general Avigdor Lieberman and Justice Minister Tsahi Hanegbi might be charged.

"I want to believe and hope that common sense will prevail here and this affair will end without charges being brought against any of the people you've mentioned and this affair will be behind us," Naveh told the radio.
Bar-On resigned less than a day after taking office in January under criticism he was professionally unfit for the post.

An Israel Channel One television report then alleged that a member of the Shas religious party, Aryeh Deri -- a kingmaker in Netanyahu's coalition who has been on trial for the last three years for corruption -- pushed the government to appoint Bar-On in the hope of winning a plea bargain.
The affair has complicated talk of a coalition government with the opposition Labour party, which says there can be no concrete moves before the investigation is over.
